heroIntro: In contemporary Bangladeshi marital disputes, allegations of dowry demands are frequently manufactured as retaliatory weapons during divorce negotiations, property disagreements, or emotional estrangement. Disgruntled spouses and their families routinely file criminal complaints dragging not only the husband but also his elderly parents, married sisters, and overseas relatives into protracted criminal proceedings. Recognizing this rampant misuse, parliament enacted the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 (যৌতুক নিরোধ আইন, ২০১৮). While Section 3 punishes genuine dowry demands, Section 5 established an aggressive counter-measure: anyone who files a false, baseless dowry case to harm an innocent person faces up to five years of rigorous imprisonment and criminal fines.

quickAnswer.title: How Can You Defend Against a False Dowry Case in Bangladesh?
quickAnswer.text: Defending against a false dowry case requires immediate procedural action: first, obtain anticipatory bail from the High Court Division under Section 498 CrPC or surrender before the Chief Judicial / Metropolitan Magistrate Court under Section 497 CrPC to prevent wrongful arrest. Next, compile primary documentary evidence—such as registered Nikahnama dower records, communication histories, and financial transfers—disproving any unlawful dowry demand. If the complaint contains frivolous allegations against distant in-laws, petition the High Court under Section 561A CrPC to quash the proceedings. Upon securing an acquittal at trial, invoke Section 5 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 to prosecute the complainant for filing a malicious false case, carrying up to five years of imprisonment.
highlights: Section 5 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 punishes false complainants with up to 5 years imprisonment.
Magistrate Courts possess discretion to grant regular bail for accused husbands and family members.
Omnibus allegations against distant in-laws can be quashed under Section 561A CrPC.
Acquitted defendants can pursue criminal counter-cases and civil damages for malicious prosecution.

sections.title: 1. The 2018 Legal Transformation: Why Section 5 Was Introduced
sections.content:
For decades, the Dowry Prohibition Act 1980 served as the primary statutory instrument penalizing the giving, taking, or demanding of dowry in Bangladesh. However, over time, the criminal courts observed an overwhelming pattern of weaponization: whenever a marriage broke down due to emotional incompatibility, extra-marital affairs, or differences over domestic living arrangements, complainants routinely added allegations of cash or car dowry demands to force financial settlements.

To curb this widespread abuse of the judicial process, parliament repealed the 1980 enactment and promulgated the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 (Act No. XXXV of 2018). While preserving stringent penalties for genuine dowry demands under Section 3 and Section 4, the legislature introduced a revolutionary deterrent mechanism in Section 5.

Under Section 5 of the 2018 Act, filing a fabricated dowry complaint is recognized as a serious independent criminal offence. The statutory provision specifically aims to protect innocent citizens, their aging parents, and collateral relatives from the indignity of unwarranted arrest, public humiliation, and financial extortion.

sections.title: 2. Statutory Ingredients: Demanding Dowry (Section 3) vs. False Complaints (Section 5)
sections.content:
A successful legal defense requires a precise understanding of the statutory definitions established in the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018. Under Section 2 of the Act, 'dowry' (যৌতুক) is defined as any property, valuable security, or money demanded directly or indirectly as consideration for marriage from one party to the other. Crucially, voluntary wedding gifts, dower (Denmohar), and traditional maintenance are expressly excluded from the definition of dowry.

Section 3 establishes that if any party to a marriage demands any dowry directly or indirectly from the other party, their parents, or guardians, such person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five (5) years, or a fine up to 50,000 BDT, or both.

In contrast, Section 5 establishes an identical maximum penalty for bad-faith litigants: if any person files or causes to be filed any complaint or case alleging an offence under the Act, knowing that there are no just or lawful grounds for making such charge, with the intent to injure or cause financial or reputational damage to another person, they shall be punished with imprisonment up to five (5) years, or a fine up to 50,000 BDT, or both.

sections.title: 3. Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 vs. Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000
sections.content:
Complainants seeking extreme judicial leverage frequently choose between the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 and the more severe Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000 (Prevention of Repression Against Women and Children Act). Understanding the operational boundaries between these enactments is vital for defense counsel.

Under Section 11(ga) of the Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000, if a husband or his relatives cause simple hurt (physical assault) to a woman for non-payment of dowry, the offence carries imprisonment from one to three years and is tried before the specialized Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal. In contrast, cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 do not require physical violence; they criminalize the mere demand or agreement for dowry and are adjudicated by the Court of Judicial Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate.

Complainants frequently attempt to inflate a verbal disagreement into a Section 11(ga) tribunal case by procuring fabricated medical injury certificates. When defense counsel proves that no physical assault occurred and that medical records are manufactured, the tribunal acquits the accused or transfers the case to the regular Magistrate Court, exposing the complainant to counter-prosecution. For trial nuances, review our analysis on stopping false criminal cases in Bangladesh.

sections.title: 4. Securing Liberty: Regular and Anticipatory Bail Strategies
sections.content:
When an accused husband or family member learns that a dowry complaint has been filed—either as an FIR at a police station or as a Complaint Register (CR) case before the Magistrate—safeguarding liberty is the immediate imperative.

Under Section 8 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018, offences under Section 3 and Section 4 are classified as cognizable, bailable, and compoundable. Despite being classified as bailable, Magistrate Courts frequently exercise judicial caution during initial surrender, particularly if the complainant appears in person alleging torture or non-payment of dower.

To avoid remand or temporary custody, the defense should prepare a comprehensive bail dossier containing the Nikahnama, proof of employment or business reputation, proof of residence, and documentary evidence of prior marital discord unrelated to dowry. If the complainant has weaponized the case by adding non-bailable penal code sections or approaching the Nari o Shishu Tribunal, the accused should immediately move an anticipatory bail application before the High Court Division under Section 498 CrPC to obtain protective pre-arrest bail. For complete procedural protocols, consult our guide on anticipatory bail in Bangladesh.

sections.title: 5. Evidentiary Tactics: How to Disprove Dowry Claims During Cross-Examination
sections.content:
Winning an acquittal in a false dowry case requires aggressive, forensic cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses (PWs)—namely the complainant, her parents, and local witnesses. Because false dowry claims are almost always concocted after the marriage has broken down, they suffer from inherent chronological and factual contradictions.

Key cross-examination angles utilized by experienced trial advocates include:

  • Timeline Discrepancies: Demonstrating that the alleged dowry demand date coincided with a period when the husband was abroad, at work in another district, or when the parties were happily living together as shown by digital photographs and communications.
  • Financial Implausibility: Showing that the complainant's family lacked the financial capacity to meet the alleged multi-million BDT dowry demand, or that the husband's family possessed superior independent wealth and had no plausible economic motive to demand money.
  • Absence of Prior Complaints: Highlighting that during years of marriage, the complainant never lodged a police GD, never informed the local Ward Councillor, and never mentioned dowry until divorce notices were served under Section 7 MFLO.
  • Independent Witness Contradictions: Discrediting neighborhood or village witnesses who admit under cross-examination that they have no direct personal knowledge of any demand and merely repeated what the complainant's father told them.

sections.title: 6. Summary Matrix: Legitimate Demands, False Charges & Penalties
sections.content:
The following comparative matrix synthesizes the statutory provisions, procedural routes, and legal exposure governing dowry litigation under the 2018 enactment:

Provision Nature of Criminal Act Statutory Punishment Trial Forum & Bail Status
Section 3 (Dowry Demand) Demanding money/property as consideration for marriage Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine up to 50,000 BDT, or both Judicial Magistrate 1st Class; Bailable & Compoundable
Section 4 (Giving or Taking) Giving, taking, or abetting the transaction of dowry Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine up to 50,000 BDT, or both Judicial Magistrate 1st Class; Bailable & Compoundable
Section 5 (False Case Filing) Filing a false complaint intending to injure another person Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine up to 50,000 BDT, or both Judicial Magistrate 1st Class; Trial upon counter-complaint
Section 11(ga) Nari o Shishu Causing simple hurt/violence for dowry demand Imprisonment 1 to 3 years and fine Nari o Shishu Tribunal; Non-Bailable by default

sections.title: 7. High Court Quashing (Section 561A CrPC) for Implicated Relatives
sections.content:
A notorious feature of false dowry litigation in Bangladesh is the indiscriminate naming of the husband's extended family members. Complaints routinely accuse married sisters residing in separate households, elderly bedridden grandparents, and overseas brothers who were not even in Bangladesh on the alleged date of occurrence.

The Supreme Court of Bangladesh has repeatedly deprecated this practice of 'roping in' innocent family members. Under Section 561A of the CrPC, the High Court Division possesses inherent jurisdiction to prevent abuse of the process of any court and secure the ends of justice.

Defense counsel files a Criminal Miscellaneous petition before the High Court Division on behalf of the implicated relatives. When the petition demonstrates that the complaint contains only vague, omnibus allegations without specifying any overt act, date, or specific role played by the relatives, the High Court regularly issues a Rule Nisi staying all criminal proceedings against the collateral family members and ultimately quashes the proceedings against them. To understand the quashing procedure, explore our guide on quashing criminal cases under Section 561A CrPC.

sections.title: 8. Illustrative Scenario: Exonerating a Husband and Prosecuting the Complainant
sections.content:
To demonstrate how defense and counter-prosecution operate in practice, consider the following illustrative scenario (composite; names and details changed).

A telecommunications engineer residing in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, served his wife with a notice of talaq under Section 7 of the MFLO after discovering prolonged infidelity. In retaliation, the wife immediately filed a Complaint Register (CR) case under Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court. She falsely alleged that the husband, along with his mother and Canada-resident brother, had demanded a 20 Lakh BDT cash dowry and a Toyota sedan, threatening to divorce her if the demand was not satisfied.

The husband engaged a Supreme Court advocate. The defense first obtained anticipatory bail from the High Court Division, followed by a Section 561A petition that quashed all proceedings against the overseas brother and mother due to total lack of specific allegations. During the trial of the husband before the Metropolitan Magistrate, the defense produced flight manifests proving the husband was attending a technical conference in Singapore on the alleged date of the dowry demand, alongside WhatsApp chats confirming the dispute arose solely from infidelity.

The Magistrate passed a comprehensive judgment acquitting the husband with an express finding that the dowry allegations were fabricated for harassment. Following the acquittal, the husband filed a formal counter-complaint under Section 5 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018. The court took cognizance, issued a warrant of arrest against the former wife, and placed her on trial for malicious prosecution.

sections.title: 9. Step-by-Step Guide to Prosecuting a Malicious Complainant under Section 5
sections.content:
Securing an acquittal is vindication, but holding the false complainant accountable under Section 5 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 establishes lasting legal justice. To initiate a successful counter-prosecution, follow these structured steps:

  • Procure Certified Copy of Acquittal Judgment: Obtain the complete, certified judgment from the trial court containing express judicial observations that the allegations were groundless, unproven, or malicious.
  • Draft a Formal Complaint under Section 5: Prepare a formal complaint detailing the chronological history, the false allegations, the acquittal findings, and the financial, social, and psychological damage inflicted on the accused.
  • File CR Case in Judicial Magistrate Court: File the case before the Chief Judicial Magistrate or Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court having territorial jurisdiction over the forum where the original false case was lodged.
  • Combine with Section 211 Penal Code: Plead Section 211 of the Penal Code 1860 (false charge of offence made with intent to injure) alongside Section 5 of the 2018 Act to maximize statutory accountability.
  • Initiate Civil Suit for Damages: File a civil suit in the Joint District Judge Court claiming substantial monetary damages for malicious prosecution and defamation to recover legal fees and compensation.

faqs.question: What is Section 5 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018?
faqs.answer: Section 5 is a landmark provision that penalizes anyone who files a false dowry complaint with intent to injure or harm another person. It prescribes rigorous imprisonment for up to five years, or a fine up to 50,000 BDT, or both.

faqs.question: Is an offence under the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 bailable in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 8 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018, offences under Section 3 and Section 4 are classified as bailable and compoundable. The accused can apply for bail as a matter of right before the Magistrate upon surrender.

faqs.question: Can distant relatives and in-laws be prosecuted in a false dowry case?
faqs.answer: Complainants often falsely implicate in-laws. However, the High Court Division regularly quashes proceedings against extended family members under Section 561A of the CrPC when allegations are vague and omnibus.

faqs.question: What is the difference between dower (Denmohar) and dowry (Yautuk)?
faqs.answer: Dower (Denmohar) is a mandatory statutory right of the Muslim wife payable by the husband under Islamic law. Dowry (Yautuk) is an unlawful property demand made as consideration for marriage, which is strictly criminalized under the 2018 Act.

faqs.question: How can I prove that the dowry allegations against me are fabricated?
faqs.answer: You can prove fabrication through timeline evidence, travel records proving absence from the scene, proof of financial status, and correspondence showing the dispute arose over other matrimonial issues without any financial demands.

faqs.question: When can an acquitted husband file a Section 5 case against his former wife?
faqs.answer: The husband can file a counter-complaint under Section 5 immediately after obtaining the certified judgment of acquittal from the trial court containing findings that the original dowry allegations were false or malicious.

faqs.question: Can an overseas Bangladeshi husband be arrested for a pending dowry case upon landing in Dhaka?
faqs.answer: If a Magistrate Court has issued a warrant of arrest, immigration police may stop the traveler at the airport. Securing anticipatory bail from the High Court Division before arrival provides legal protection against arrest.

faqs.question: Can a false dowry case be settled out of court through compromise?
faqs.answer: Yes. Section 8 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 expressly classifies offences under Section 3 as compoundable. The parties can execute a compromise deed (Solenama) and have the case dismissed with court approval.
